html:
A tragedy by Aeschylus, staged in Athens in 472 BCE. It is the oldest surviving play in the world.

It tells of the Greek victory at Salamis in 480 BCE, but from the Persian side. The scene is the Persian capital, where the queen mother Atossa waits for news. A messenger describes the disaster, the ghost of her husband Darius blames the pride of their son, and at last Xerxes comes home in rags.

It is the only surviving Greek tragedy about recent history rather than myth. Many in the audience, Aeschylus among them, had fought in the wars. Yet the play does not simply cheer: it shows the enemy's grief with sympathy, and treats the defeat as a punishment for overreaching.

The young Pericles paid for the chorus as a liturgy, and the set of plays won first prize.
sum: A tragedy by Aeschylus, staged in Athens in 472 BCE. It is the oldest surviving play in the world.
